body:
Worker rule (Termal::Opus-Causal, 2026-11-23, my own slip, confirmed by Fable2 d84e975b #20): never write to the system temp folder. In the Bash tool, Git Bash's /tmp is C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Temp, OUTSIDE the repository. A throwaway `> /tmp/x` redirect therefore breaks the repository-folder rule. Scratch files go only under the repository's .tmp/ (e.g. C:/github/Personal/TermAl/.tmp/<name>), and are removed when done. Before any redirect or mktemp in a shell command, check that the target path is inside the repository.
Related trap from the same day (w-4483f709da27): a test state booted with spawning enabled (AppState::new_with_paths…_for_test), with no registered provider fixture, can launch the real `codex` from PATH. TermAl then seeds that server's Codex home from the user's, copying auth.json into the product test temp dir. Any change that routes sessions to a newly launched provider must gate that launch under cfg(test) on a registered fixture.
